IPv6 is not fundamentally more secure than IPv4 in the sense of being automatically better — both protocols rely on IPsec for security, and IPv4 can also use IPsec even if it is not mandatory there; the main difference is that IPv6 requires support for IPSec by default while IPv4 does not [d4][d1]. However, IPv6 does offer some inherent security advantages: it was designed with IPSec at its core, provides improved data integrity, and has a much larger address space that can be used to generate truly random addresses and defeat address-scanning attacks, making it more difficult for an attacker to map addresses to hosts on a network [d4][d3]. The two protocols are also not mutually exclusive — most modern systems run both IPv4 and IPv6 simultaneously, so security best practices must be applied to both stacks equally [d2].
[[END-OF-ANSWER]]

No, cycads did not dominate the Mesozoic era plant kingdom. [d1] According to paleobotanists, cycads were particularly abundant and diverse during the Mesozoic era, earning it the nickname 'the age of cycads,' while dinosaurs were the dominant animals [d1]. However, this view is contested by research that identifies Bennettitales and Nilssoniales as the actual dominant plant groups in mid-Mesozoic floras [d2], and even the famously Mesozoic plant Cycadeoidea is revealed to have been a member of the extinct Bennettitales rather than a true cycad [d3].
